2.hint: Create the throwaway data directory: mkdir -p /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown.

3.hint: Run `/usr/pgsql-16/bin/initdb -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown --data-checksums` to create the test cluster with checksums enabled.

4.hint: Open postgresql.conf with vi to change the port.

6.hint: Change it to port = 5436 and save.

8.hint: Verify with pg_isready -p 5436 - should be accepting connections.

9.hint: Start a long-running query in the background: psql -p 5436 -c "SELECT pg_sleep(300);" &

10.hint: Try a smart shutdown: pg_ctl stop -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown -m smart - it will hang, waiting on the pg_sleep client.

11.hint: Press Ctrl+C to stop watching the smart shutdown, then check pg_isready -p 5436 - it should show 'rejecting connections', not 'accepting'.

12.hint: Try a new connection - it should fail with 'FATAL: the database system is shutting down'.

13.hint: Escalate out of the stuck smart shutdown: pg_ctl stop -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown -m fast - this terminates the pg_sleep session and completes the shutdown.

14.hint: You will see the killed psql session print its own connection-lost error and the shell's job-done notification.

15.hint: Verify with pg_isready -p 5436 - should show 'no response'.

16.hint: Start the cluster again: pg_ctl start -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown -l /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown/server.log

17.hint: Write some data so there is something to replay after the crash: psql -p 5436 -c "CREATE TABLE test_write (id int); INSERT INTO test_write SELECT generate_series(1,1000);"

18.hint: Open a new background session: psql -p 5436 -c "SELECT pg_sleep(300);" &

19.hint: Perform an immediate shutdown: pg_ctl stop -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown -m immediate - almost instant, unlike smart or fast.

20.hint: Start the cluster again to trigger crash recovery: pg_ctl start -D /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown -l /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown/server.log

21.hint: Check the recovery messages in log/postgresql-*.log (not server.log - logging_collector redirects there after startup).

23.hint: Remove the throwaway data directory: rm -rf /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown

24.hint: Confirm it is gone with ls /opt/pgsql/data-shutdown - should error 'No such file or directory'.

25.hint: Confirm your main PG16 cluster on port 5432 was never affected by any of this.
